title: Maintenance of Underlying Insurance Condition, Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy
content:
**Condition.** The named insured must keep every scheduled underlying policy in force at no less than the required limit for as long as its exposure exists. When a scheduled underlying policy ends while its exposure remains, a lapse is recorded on the date coverage ended. An underlying policy is removed from the schedule only when the exposure it insured is gone (vehicle sold, property sold, watercraft sold), never merely because the policy ended.

**Replacement period.** Replacement underlying insurance scheduled no later than the replacement period that starts on the underlying lapse date keeps the umbrella in force. The replacement period is counted in calendar days from the underlying lapse date, and scheduling on the last day is on time. Its length is the tier's replacement period.

**Notice and rescission.** After that period a notice of cancellation for underlying not maintained is issued with a scheduled cancellation date the tier's underlying notice period later, and it is rescinded when qualifying replacement underlying is scheduled before that date.

These dates are read from the schedule of underlying insurance of the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy: the lapse entry for the underlying policy number and its lapse date.

## Lapse or removal

| What happened to the scheduled underlying policy | Entry on the schedule |
|---|---|
| The policy ended (cancelled or expired) and its exposure remains | A lapse, dated the day coverage ended |
| The exposure the policy insured is gone (vehicle, property or watercraft sold) | A removal from the schedule |

A policy that has merely ended is never removed from the schedule; it stays on the schedule with a lapse recorded against it.

## Umbrella status through a lapse

| Stage | Status of the umbrella |
|---|---|
| Lapse recorded; replacement scheduled on or before the last day of the replacement period | Stays in force |
| Replacement period passes with no replacement scheduled; notice issued | Pending cancellation, with a scheduled cancellation date |
| Qualifying replacement scheduled before the scheduled cancellation date | The notice is rescinded and the umbrella returns to in force |
| Scheduled cancellation date arrives with no replacement | Cancelled |

## Timeline (hypothetical dates)

A hypothetical underlying policy lapses on 1 March, on a tier with a 30-day replacement period and a 30-day notice period.

- The replacement period runs in calendar days from 1 March; its last day is 31 March. Replacement scheduled on 31 March is on time and keeps the umbrella in force.
- With no replacement by 31 March, the period has passed on 1 April; the notice for underlying not maintained is issued after the period, on 1 April or later.
- A notice issued on 3 April carries a scheduled cancellation date 30 days later, 3 May. Qualifying replacement scheduled on 2 May, before 3 May, rescinds the notice.

## Basis questions

**Does a replacement have to meet the required limit?** Yes: the replacement that rescinds a notice is qualifying replacement underlying, and every scheduled underlying policy is kept at no less than the required limit.

**Can a notice for underlying not maintained be issued during the replacement period?** No; it is issued after that period.
